assessment: Taking joint drumming as a model of collective dynamics, and combining solid quantitative methods, the authors characterize how human behavior changes, at the individual- and group-level, as a function of group numerosity. A take-home message of this important work is that not everything we know from studies involving dyads should be necessarily generalized to larger groups. This study will be of great interest to scientists looking for new approaches to understanding group behavior, especially within the fields of human cognition, neurosciences, and musicology.
